ja: 来られるかどうか、分かる？
en: Do you know if you can come?
alternatives: Do you know whether you can make it?
Have you figured out if you can come?
point: 間接疑問の if 節は平叙文の語順

ja: 私が伏せた事情が今は誘いの支障だ。
en: What I concealed now complicates the invitation.
alternatives: My undisclosed circumstances now complicate the invitation.
The facts I withheld now complicate the invitation.
point: what I concealed で、私が過去に伏せた事情を指す。

ja: ねえ、無理に誘わせないでよ。
en: Don't make me twist your arm.
alternatives: Don't make me beg you to come.
Don't make me pressure you into coming.
point: make + 人 + 原形。twist one's arm は強引に説得する

ja: まだ席があるよ。
en: There are still seats.
alternatives: There are seats left.
We still have seats.
point: 数えられる複数なら there are

ja: ずっと誘おうと思ってた。
en: I've been meaning to invite you.
alternatives: I've been meaning to ask you out.
I've been meaning to invite you over.
point: 「ずっと〜しようと思ってた」は have been meaning to

ja: 出かける気分じゃないんだ。
en: I don't feel like going out.
alternatives: I'm not really up for going out.
I'm not in the mood to go out.
point: feel like の後ろは -ing

ja: 昨日カイを誘ったよ。
en: I invited Kai yesterday.
alternatives: Yesterday I invited Kai.
I asked Kai to come yesterday.
point: invite は規則動詞で過去形は invited

ja: みんな、遊びに来て。
en: Everyone, come visit me.
alternatives: Everyone, come over.
Everyone, come see me.
point: come visit me は私に会いに来てという誘い。

ja: 私は今回は遠慮したいんだけど。
en: I'd rather bow out this time.
alternatives: I'd prefer to decline this time.
I'd rather sit this one out.
point: would rather と bow out で辞退の希望を柔らかく伝える。

ja: 来るかどうか教えて。
en: Tell me if you're coming.
alternatives: Let me know if you can come.
Let me know whether you're coming.
point: 「かどうか」は if か whether

ja: 今夜、空いてる？
en: Are you free tonight?
alternatives: Are you free this evening?
Do you have plans tonight?
point: 「空いてる」は be free

ja: 今夜は友達と外食するんだ。
en: I'm eating out with friends tonight.
alternatives: I'm dining out with friends tonight.
I'm meeting friends for dinner tonight.
point: 決まった予定は現在進行形で言える

ja: 私はその誘いを見送るよ。
en: I'll pass on that invitation.
alternatives: I'll decline that invitation.
I'll turn down that invitation.
point: pass on an invitation は誘いを見送る。

ja: 私と一緒に来てよ。
en: Come with me.
alternatives: Come along with me.
Join me.
point: 命令文は主語を付けず動詞から始める

ja: 時間が許せば、あとで合流するよ。
en: Time permitting, I'll join you later.
alternatives: If time allows, I'll join you later.
If I have time, I'll join you later.
point: Time permitting は「時間が許せば」の分詞構文

ja: 日曜にパーティーだよ。
en: There's a party Sunday.
alternatives: We're having a party Sunday.
A party is on Sunday.
point: 「〜がある」は there is

ja: 私はもう出席すると伝えた。
en: I've already confirmed my attendance.
alternatives: I've already said that I'll attend.
I've already confirmed that I'm coming.
point: 現在完了で参加の意思を伝え済みと表す。

ja: カイに来てと頼まれた。
en: Kai asked me to come.
alternatives: Kai asked me to come over.
I was asked by Kai to come.
point: ask 人 to do で「人に〜するよう頼む」

ja: 断ってたら私は今ごろ仲間外れだ。
en: Had I declined, I'd be left out now.
alternatives: If I'd declined, I'd be excluded now.
I'd be excluded now if I'd declined.
point: 過去の辞退が今の仲間外れにつながる仮定。

ja: 先週、彼に誘われたよ。
en: He invited me last week.
alternatives: Last week he invited me.
He invited me out last week.
point: 日本語は受け身でも英語は he を主語に

ja: 君は誰を誘ってる？
en: Who are you inviting?
alternatives: Who are you asking along?
Who are you inviting over?
point: who で招待する相手を尋ねる。

ja: 彼が来るか、ミカは知ってると思う？
en: Do you think Mika knows if he's coming?
alternatives: Do you think Mika knows whether he's coming?
Would Mika know if he's coming, do you think?
point: Do you think の後は平叙文の語順

ja: どこで会おうか？
en: Where should we meet?
alternatives: Where shall we meet?
Where can we meet?
point: 場所を聞くなら where で始める

ja: 今夜、うちに遊びに来ない？
en: Why don't you come over tonight?
alternatives: Do you want to come over tonight?
Want to come over tonight?
point: come over は「家に来る」。Why don't you ~? は誘い

ja: 雨が降っても、私は行くよ。
en: I'll go even if it rains.
alternatives: Even if it rains, I'll go.
I'll come even if it's raining.
point: 未来のことでも even if の後ろは現在形

ja: 電話の時には、もう食べてた。
en: I'd already eaten when you called.
alternatives: I had already eaten when you called.
You called after I'd already eaten.
point: 電話より前のことは過去完了

ja: 来てくれたらと思ってたんだ。
en: I was hoping you'd come along.
alternatives: I was hoping you could join us.
I was wondering if you'd come along.
point: was hoping で控えめな誘いになる

ja: ミカが、君も誘えって言ってたよ。
en: Mika told me to invite you too.
alternatives: Mika asked me to invite you too.
Mika wanted me to invite you as well.
point: tell + 人 + to do で言われた内容を伝える

ja: この招待で私の複雑な思いが蘇る。
en: This invitation brings back my mixed feelings.
alternatives: This invitation revives my mixed feelings.
This invitation stirs up my old mixed feelings.
point: bring back my mixed feelings は以前の複雑な思いが再び湧くことを表す。

ja: 行けたらいいのになあ。
en: I wish I could make it.
alternatives: If only I could make it.
I wish I were able to come.
point: 現実と違う願いは wish + could。make it は「行ける」

ja: 参加費は会費に含まれる。
en: Admission's included in membership fees.
alternatives: Membership fees cover admission.
The membership fee includes admission.
point: is included で費用に含まれると伝える。

ja: 私が断ってたら今の気まずさはないのに。
en: Had I declined, I wouldn't feel awkward now.
alternatives: If I'd declined, I wouldn't feel uncomfortable now.
I wouldn't feel awkward now if I'd declined.
point: Had I declined は過去に断っていた場合を置き、今の気まずさがない結果と結ぶ。

ja: ぜひ行きたいです。
en: I'd love to go.
alternatives: I'd love to come.
I'd like to go.
point: 「行きたい」は would love to + 動詞

ja: 私、車で送れるよ。
en: I can drive you there.
alternatives: I can give you a ride.
I can take you by car.
point: can で可能な手助けを申し出る。

ja: 空いていれば、ぜひ行くんだけど。
en: I'd love to, if I were free.
alternatives: If I were free, I'd love to come.
If I weren't busy, I'd love to.
point: 現実と違う仮定は if + were、主節は would

ja: 誘ってくれてたら、行けたのに。
en: If you'd asked, I could've gone.
alternatives: I could have gone if you'd asked.
Had you asked, I could have gone.
If you'd invited me, I could have gone.
point: 過去の仮定は had + 過去分詞、could have + 過去分詞

ja: 君を誘い忘れなければよかった。
en: I wish I hadn't overlooked you.
alternatives: I wish I'd remembered to invite you.
If only I'd remembered to invite you.
point: wish + 過去完了で、招待し忘れた過去を悔やむ。

ja: 彼が丁寧に断れないと思ってるか気になる。
en: I wonder whether he feels he can't graciously decline.
alternatives: I wonder if he feels unable to decline politely.
I'm wondering whether he feels he can't tactfully refuse.
point: 相手が感じている内容を whether の節の中に入れる。

ja: 私の沈黙は同意扱いだと彼女は言った。
en: She said my silence would pass for tacit consent.
alternatives: She said my silence would be taken as consent.
She said silence would be interpreted as my consent.
point: tacit consent は言葉にせず示した同意。

ja: 一番来てほしいのは、君なんだよ。
en: It's you I most want to come.
alternatives: You're the one I most want to come.
You're the one I'd most love to see there.
point: It's you (that) で人を強調。that は省ける

ja: 同伴者もいいですか？
en: May I bring a guest?
alternatives: Could I bring someone along?
Would bringing a guest be okay?
point: May I は丁寧に許可を求める。

ja: 私の返事は参加を濁してたかも。
en: My reply might've sounded evasive about coming.
alternatives: My response may have sounded noncommittal about coming.
My answer might have seemed evasive about attending.
point: evasive は返事をはぐらかす感じを表す。

ja: 終わったら合流するよ。
en: I'll join you when I'm done.
alternatives: I'll meet you once I'm done.
I'll join you once I finish work.
point: 未来のことでも when 節は現在形

ja: 私は誘いを滅多に見送らない。
en: Rarely do I pass up an invitation.
alternatives: I rarely turn down an invitation.
I seldom decline an invitation.
point: rarely を先頭に出すと do が主語の前。

ja: 断れそうもない誘いを私に断らせないで。
en: Don't make me decline what feels impossible to refuse.
alternatives: Don't force me to reject what I can't refuse.
Don't make me refuse an invitation I can't decline.
point: make me decline と what の節で断れない圧力を表す。

ja: 前に話したバンド、観に行こう。
en: Let's see the band I mentioned.
alternatives: Let's go see the band I mentioned.
Let's see that band I told you about.
point: the band の後ろに I mentioned を続ける

ja: 私なら、その誘いは受けるよ。
en: If I were you, I'd say yes.
alternatives: I'd say yes if I were you.
I'd accept the invitation if I were you.
point: If I were you で「私なら」とアドバイス

ja: 私、招待客の意向を探り続けてる。
en: I've been sounding out guests.
alternatives: I've been gauging guests' wishes.
I've been asking guests what they want.
point: sound out は相手の意向を探る。

ja: 断ると関係を損なうか私は知りたい。
en: I want to know if refusing hurts relations.
alternatives: I'd like to know if refusing hurts relations.
I'm wondering whether refusing harms relationships.
point: if の節で、断ることが関係を損なうかを尋ねる。

ja: 雨でなければ、みんなを誘ったのに。
en: If it hadn't rained, I'd have invited everyone.
alternatives: I'd have invited everyone if it hadn't rained.
Had it not rained, I would've invited everyone.
point: 過去の仮定は had + 過去分詞、would have + 過去分詞

ja: もう夕飯は食べたの？
en: Have you had dinner yet?
alternatives: Have you eaten yet?
Have you eaten dinner yet?
point: 「もう〜した？」は現在完了 + yet

ja: 私は彼を昼食に誘い込んだ。
en: I roped him into lunch.
alternatives: I talked him into lunch.
I persuaded him to come to lunch.
point: rope 人 into はうまく誘って参加させる。

ja: 君の招待では本音を言う余地はほぼない。
en: Your invitation leaves me little room for candor.
alternatives: Your invitation gives me little scope for frankness.
Your invitation leaves me hardly any room for honesty.
point: candor は遠慮せず率直に話すことを表し数えない。

ja: 私はぜひ君に一緒に来てほしい。
en: I'm keen to have you along.
alternatives: I'd love you to come along.
I'm keen for you to join me.
point: keen to はぜひしたいという気持ち。

ja: 氷とレモン一個、持ってきてくれる？
en: Could you bring some ice and a lemon?
alternatives: Can you bring ice and a lemon?
Could you bring a bit of ice and a lemon?
point: 氷は数えられず、レモンは a lemon

ja: 夕食より昼食が都合いい。
en: Lunch works better than dinner.
alternatives: Lunch is more convenient than dinner.
Lunch suits me better than dinner.
point: works better は予定の都合がよりよい。

ja: 駅前のあの店、行ってみようよ。
en: Let's try the place by the station.
alternatives: How about trying the place by the station?
Want to try the place by the station?
point: 名詞の後ろに前置詞句を置いて修飾

ja: 早く来たほうがいいよ。
en: You should come early.
alternatives: You should get here early.
It's best to come early.
point: 「〜したほうがいい」は should
